pairs.question: Ubi ea est, opsecro?
pairs.answer: Eccam in tabellis porrectam: in cera cubat.
pairs.derivation: Calidorus asks where his girlfriend is (after Pseudolus says 'Tuam amicam video, Calidore'); Pseudolus answers she is there in the writing-tablets. Stripped speaker labels (CAL., PS.) and the inline verse number 35. Real interrogative answered directly.

pairs.question: Quid ita?
pairs.derivation: Calidorus asks why so (Pseudolus had said he cannot squeeze out a tear); Pseudolus answers that his family was always dry-eyed. Stripped speaker labels. The 'why-because' relation is genuine: interrogative answered with a real reason.

pairs.question: Sed quid ea drachuma facere vis?
pairs.derivation: Pseudolus asks what Calidorus wants to do with the drachma he requested; Calidorus answers he wants to buy a rope. Stripped speaker labels and the line break. 'sed' is the author's connective (utterance, not a speech tag) so kept. Real interrogative answered directly. Did NOT extend into the follow-up 'Quam ob rem? / Qui me faciam pensilem' because that secondary question is too context-dependent to stand alone.

pairs.question: Cur id ausu's facere?
pairs.derivation: Calidorus asks Ballio why he dared sell the girl; Ballio answers it pleased him, she was his. Stripped speaker labels (CAL., BAL.). Stopped the answer before 'CAL. Eho, Pseudole...' which turns to a new action. Real interrogative answered directly.

pairs.question: Quid opus gladio?
pairs.derivation: Calidorus orders a sword brought; Pseudolus asks what need there is of a sword; Calidorus answers, so that he may kill Ballio and himself. Stripped speaker labels (PS., CAL.). Real interrogative answered with purpose clause.

pairs.question: Venitne homo ad te?
pairs.derivation: Simo asks Ballio whether the man (Pseudolus's agent) came to him; Ballio answers no. Stripped speaker labels (SIM., BAL.) and the surrounding stichomythic 'Quid est?' tags. Yes/no interrogative answered with a complete negation.
